description: Layer 1 (normalisation) and layer 2 (canonicalisation-at-extraction) fixtures for WS5's skill/qualification matching. These pairs were originally miscategorised as embedding true_match cases in the WS6.1 v1 calibration run, which produced an 80-93% false-negative rate purely as a labelling artefact: an abbreviation shares almost no characters with its expansion, so a general-purpose embedding model cannot be expected to see them as equivalent. Neither layer runs at scoring time -- both resolve to a plain string BEFORE scoring, so by the time the JS engine (5.3) compares a CV skill against a requirement, this has already been handled: match is checked at layer 1 (deterministic normalisation, no LLM) first, and if that fails, both the CV and the vacancy requirement were already canonicalised to the same target string at extraction/save time (layer 2), so it becomes an exact match too. Only genuine cross-vocabulary equivalence reaches the embedding layer (layer 3, skills-pairs.json / qualifications-pairs.json). Not run by calibrate-thresholds.mjs -- this is reference data for the WS4 extraction prompt and the vacancy-save canonicalisation step, not a similarity-threshold measurement. A deterministic-match test harness (not embeddings) should be built alongside that implementation.

layer_1_normalisation.note: Pure JS string rules -- case, punctuation, suffix, version number. No LLM call.

pairs.rule: suffix normalisation (kept .js as the canonical form here, opposite direction from React -- Node.js is the more universally recognised full name; React is more commonly written bare)

layer_2_canonicalisation_at_extraction.note: Extraction model expands/normalises to one canonical form. Runs once per CV and once per vacancy save -- both sides must go through it or the exact-match check at scoring time silently fails.

degree_type_canonicalisation.note: Degree TYPE strings that name the SAME field and the SAME structural level (5.4's 6/7/8 rule already treats them as equivalent level-wise) -- these never reach the field-only embedding comparison because the type prefix is stripped before comparison, not because the embedding model resolves them.

whole_name_abbreviation.note: The whole degree title is an abbreviation or alternate naming convention, not just the type prefix. Field + level both come out of this step.
